title: R6 through R12 residence districts (flat ZR 23-22 rows) - maximum residential floor area ratio (standard residences)
description: DRAFT extraction (needs_review) of the maximum residential floor area ratio for standard residences in the FLAT (non-wide-street-conditional) R6 through R12 districts of the ZR 23-22 table. This rule covers every ZR 23-22 district whose standard value is a single table lookup; the four districts that ZR 23-22 footnote 1 conditions on wide-street proximity (R6, R7-1, R7-2, R8) are handled by a separate rule (r6-r7-r8-wide-street-conditional-far) and are intentionally excluded here. NOT a Verified determination - a candidate representation awaiting raw-HTML source verification and G6 qualified-human legal approval. The engine computes the standard-residences FAR and the resulting maximum residential floor area from the lot area; the higher qualifying-affordable-housing / qualifying-senior-housing FAR (the ZR 23-22 second column) is surfaced as a conditional alternative (never silently applied). effective_from is the section's Last Amended date (2024-12-05): evaluating as_of an earlier date yields a visible not-effective outcome.

citations.quote: MAXIMUM FLOOR AREA RATIO FOR R6-R12 DISTRICTS. Separate maximum residential floor area ratios are set forth for zoning lots containing standard residences and zoning lots containing qualifying affordable housing or qualifying senior housing.

inputs.name: zoning_district
inputs.description: The residence district governing the lot (or the portion under evaluation). District SCOPE is enforced by applicability (in_set the flat ZR 23-22 rows), NOT by an input domain enum: a district outside this set - including the wide-street-conditional R6/R7-1/R7-2/R8 handled by their own rule - is a visible not_applicable. An uncertain M2-T013 geometric assignment is passed via spatial_context and downgrades coverage.

inputs.name: lot_area_sq_ft
inputs.description: Zoning-lot area in square feet; must be strictly positive. A zero/negative/non-finite value is rejected fail-closed (professional_review_required, no computed value).

inputs.name: housing_program
inputs.description: Whether the lot contains standard residences or qualifying affordable / qualifying senior housing (the two ZR 23-22 columns). When absent, the qualifying-housing alternative is surfaced as conditional (not decided) - whether a development qualifies is a separate legal determination.

outputs.name: max_residential_far
outputs.description: Maximum residential floor area ratio for standard residences in the district (ZR 23-22 first column).

outputs.name: max_residential_floor_area_sq_ft
outputs.description: Maximum residential floor area = lot area x FAR.

parameters.name: standard_far_by_district
parameters.note: Standard-residences maximum residential FAR (ZR 23-22 first column) for every flat R6-R12 district. Candidate values pending raw-HTML verification and G6 approval.

parameters.name: qualifying_far_by_district
parameters.note: Qualifying affordable-housing / qualifying senior-housing maximum residential FAR (ZR 23-22 second column). SURFACED as the conditional alternative (see the qualifying_housing exception), never applied by this rule: whether a development qualifies is a separate legal determination. Provenance-linked here so the value is byte-checkable against the snapshot; deliberately not consumed by a computation step.

steps.note: Select the standard-residences maximum residential FAR for the district (ZR 23-22 first column).
Maximum residential floor area = lot area (sq ft) x FAR.

exceptions.description: A higher maximum residential floor area ratio (the ZR 23-22 second column) applies to zoning lots containing qualifying affordable housing or qualifying senior housing. The full per-district qualifying FAR (matching the qualifying_far_by_district parameter, each value byte-verified against the snapshot) is: R6A 3.90, R6-1 3.90, R7B 3.90, R6B 2.40, R6D 3.00, R6-2 3.00, R7A 5.01, R7D 5.60, R7X 6.00, R7-3 6.00, R8A 7.20, R8X 7.20, R8B 4.80, R9A 9.02, R9 9.02, R9D 10.80, R9X 10.80, R9-1 10.80, R10A 12.00, R10X 12.00, R10 12.00, R11 15.00, R12 18.00. Whether a development qualifies is a separate legal determination and is not decided by this rule; when the housing program is unknown or qualifying, the result is conditional and the higher FAR may apply.
exceptions.note: Surfaced, never collapsed: the standard-residences FAR is reported with an explicit conditional flag that a qualifying-housing FAR may govern.

special_district_interactions.description: Special Purpose Districts (ZR Articles VIII-XIV) and other mapped overlays may modify residence-district floor area. When a mapped special district applies, its provisions govern and must be evaluated by the corresponding special rule; this general rule does not apply the modification.

uncertainty_policy.note: An uncertain, split, sliver, or invalid M2-T013 geometric district assignment is never collapsed into a single definitive district: coverage is downgraded to professional_review_required (or data_conflict) and the geometric uncertainty is recorded in the trace.

limitations: Draft extraction pending raw-HTML source verification and G6 qualified-human legal approval; not a Verified determination.
Only the standard-residences residential FAR is computed; the qualifying affordable / senior housing FAR (ZR 23-22 second column) is surfaced (conditional), not computed.
The four wide-street-conditional districts R6, R7-1, R7-2 and R8 are out of scope for this rule and are handled by r6-r7-r8-wide-street-conditional-far.
Special Purpose District and other overlay modifications are not applied.
